result:
Round 113 is done on my side: a touch press no longer jumps the Volume, Pan, Master or group Volume faders. The bug (A-R38-REVIEW-TOUCH) stays open until C's browser checks pass.

**The fix**
- The shared `useRelativeFaderDrag` hook now returns `{ onPointerDown, ref }`. The `ref` attaches a native `touchstart` listener on the input itself with `{ passive: false }`, and it only calls `preventDefault()`.
- The listener is attached when the input mounts and removed when the input unmounts or is swapped, for example when a lane is folded.
- Because the guard is part of the hook, it covers all four relative-drag faders, including the video track's Volume. A future fader built on the hook gets it automatically.
- The pointerdown drag logic is unchanged.
- I touched only the six files B allowed:
  - `useRelativeFaderDrag.ts`;
  - `ArrangementLane.tsx`, where Pan's existing ref is merged with the new one without a type assertion;
  - `ArrangementMaster.tsx`;
  - `ArrangementGroupHeader.tsx`;
  - the new `fader-touch.test.tsx`;
  - the new doc 097.
- Zoom, `fader.ts`, the context, CSS and every protected or existing test file are unchanged. The frozen list checks out at the start and at the end.

**Tests and checks**
- The new test file has 7 tests (FT1–FT7). I added FT7 after the review: it covers fold/unfold, where the same hook gets a new input element.
- Each test file was run against deliberately broken versions of the hook, then the hook was restored and confirmed identical:
  - no `preventDefault()`: 5 tests fail;
  - `passive: true`: 6 fail;
  - no removal of the old listener: 2 fail;
  - no listener options: 2 fail;
  - an unstable Pan ref: 2 fail.
- Typecheck and lint pass, and Biome is clean on the five code and test files.
- The new file plus the 8 neighbouring fader and mixer test files: 167 tests pass, 0 fail.
- I did not run the full suite or `verify`; the root gate runs those.

**Code review:** the code-reviewer agent scored it 8.5/10, with no Critical or High findings.
- I fixed the Medium (fold/unfold had no test) and two of the Lows (one test assertion could pass when the listener had no options, and the doc overstated what two tests prove).
- One Low was already accepted by B: a double tap on touch no longer resets a fader.
- Its architecture note for B, verbatim: "Keep: it is the same element and the same gesture concern, an idempotent five-line callback covered by FT3/FT4, and splitting it out would add a second hook that new faders could forget to use. No proposal for the planner."

**Browser self-check (Chromium, 1440, one run each; not a substitute for C)**
- Zoom still jumps (678 → 63), so the probe does reach the native slider.
- Volume, Pan and Master no longer move on touchStart.
- A touch drag moves each one in the drag direction, within the expected range, with one history entry each.
- A tap changes nothing and adds no history entry.
- There were 0 console errors and 0 forbidden requests. The first probe attempt crashed on page setup. A check right after showed the page healthy, and the rerun was clean; it was probably the dev server reloading my changed files.

**Not verified by me, left for C:** the group and video Volume faders in the browser, 1280×720, the 3-run series, Ctrl+Z after a touch drag, the double-tap info row and the mouse and keyboard rows. The reviewer also thinks a long press may no longer open the context menu on these faders; that is the same mechanism as the accepted double-tap change, so I left it for B.

Everything is in `tmp/studio-real-loop/a-round-113.md`, with the evidence files in `tmp/studio-real-loop/a-round-113/`.
